scope: Wave-cut rock benches and scarps on erosion-dominated ocean shores, sharing existing terrain and water.
status: Static landform retained after revised numerical, native and moving-camera checks. Broader art quality and frame tails remain unfinished.

sources.application: Differentiate wave-eroded resistant rock shores from sediment-rich beaches and sheltered deposits.

implementation: Static metre-addressed regional wave-exposure proxy, inherited relief, rock hardness and sediment supply control admission.
Monotone shallow platform/scarp profile preserves sea zero; no closed tide basin, displaced ocean or decorative water ribbon.
Explicit bare-rock mask reaches soil depth, organic matter, terrain/map/channel materials, rooted scatter and ground cover.
Sandy coves and bars retain the earlier depositional profile outside the admitted rock coast.
No new frame tick, scenery object, draw call, texture sample or shader pass. Existing terrain query does the scalar shaping.

rejected_review.reason: The first profile made an almost invisible shelf on steep headlands. One along-shore camera also stood on submerged seabed. Neither is accepted as successful visual evidence.
rejected_review.revision: Broaden inherited height band for wave erosion, keep upper/deep ground unchanged, require a walkable bench for review discovery, and hold coastal review cameras above the sea surface.

native.review: Ground and along-shore views show a walkable exposed bench below the inherited headland. Elevated view shows the connected shelf and ocean. No extra ocean sheet, visible gaps or underwater review camera.
native.limitations: The physical form is improved; bare rock surface remains too uniform and the surrounding existing terrain/vegetation art is not fully accepted.

performance.conditions: 1920x1080, Medium vegetation, 6km, same actual world/coordinate; 60s moving 180m loop plus rapid turns, fresh ordinary Mono nondevelopment processes, uncontended and all frames focused.
performance.assessment: Mixed frame tails: higher average and fewer frames over16.7ms, worse p95/p99 and more over10ms. Shape cost increases about0.0014ms per frame. No general renderer or stutter improvement claim.
performance.limits: Physical terrain and visible geometry differ; the old route ends underwater beside its steep shore. Neither moving scene is fully settled. This tests practical traversal of the changed coast, not equal-geometry rendering or global performance.

limits: Long-term wave exposure is a geographic proxy rather than a physical wave-energy simulation.
A heightfield cannot form overhangs, detached sea arches or caves.
No claim of a universal 100 FPS floor; the moving/turning comparison remains mixed.
Two numerical sites in one world do not establish global distribution or complete coast variety.
